rationales.1: Named seasonal shelves plus a per-card sowing window make season fit structural rather than something to hunt for, and price and stock sit in a fixed place on every card. The lone view-packet button on a single card breaks the row rhythm and implies only that packet is browsable.
rationales.2: Price, stock language, quantity field and add-to-basket all follow ordinary commerce convention, with delivery terms stated beside the buy control. Nothing clever intrudes on the money path.
rationales.3: The null-price packet shows an italic price-on-request line with the reason in the body copy, the estimated germination figure is labelled twice, and out of stock is unmissable. The UK-only shipping badge sits high on both surfaces, well before any purchase intent.
rationales.4: Names, descriptions and prices are set generously and nothing depends on hover. The growing meta line that older gardeners most need is the smallest and palest text on the card.
rationales.5: The packet frame, dashed label rule and botanical glyph repeat faithfully across both surfaces as one system. Card interiors do not align across a row, so dashed rules and prices land at four different heights, and the product page leaves a large empty left column.
rationales.6: Buy box first, then the year table, difficulty, potting-shed notes and companion packets with their own prices and stock, so a first-time gardener can decide in one pass. The difficulty and germination line is repeated below the table with no added information.
rationales.7: The rack by the shop door, shelf by shelf: the shop is a physical seed rack and every product is a packet on it, carried by the section headings, the packet frames and the card structure alike. It reads as two growers stocking their own rack rather than borrowed boutique polish.
rationales.8: The break is entirely the rack-and-packet conceit and the drawn botanicals, both squarely in the brand layer. Price, stock, quantity and add-to-basket are left completely conventional.
rationales.9: Two of us keep it stocked; from our potting shed; good company for it; fussy about damp, for the patient gardener — warm, specific and unhurried throughout. No competitor could publish this copy unchanged.
rationales.10: Stock state is on every card and the shelf sections answer what is sowable now before any filtering is needed. There is no newly-in-stock or freshness cue for someone checking back.
